decisionsTitle: «Traseul»: Strava and Garmin Connect, each a link and a map behind a press, and an uploaded GPX
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-11**, pasting a Garmin Connect course embed (an `<iframe>` to the course's embed address) and a Strava route embed (a `<div class="strava-embed-placeholder" data-embed-type="route" data-embed-id=… data-style=… data-map-hash=… data-token=…>` and `<script src=…/embed.js>`): «so basically I need to put all: Garmin Connect embedded, Strava embedded, Garmin Connect link, Strava link AND GPX file», and the layout: «so I will have Garmin Connect / Strava in tabs and GPX file at the bottom of them».

Amends §61 (a Strava map is now drawn — behind a press, as an iframe built from the id — and Strava's script still never runs), §69 and §110 (the facade rule now covers maps), §332 and §387 (the route's links and files), and `AGENTS.md` §17 (one stored object that is not a picture) and §18.3.

**Decision.**

- *Two columns on the event, expand only (migration `0142_route_maps_and_gpx`).* `events.route_maps` is `[{ provider, id, style?, mapHash?, token? }]`, at most one Strava route and one Garmin Connect course; `events.route_gpx` is `{ key, name, size, uploadedAt }`. Both are facts of the event, the same in both languages, and a series edit, a repeat and a duplicate carry them like the route (§49, §130). Two CHECKs hold the shape at the database: a known provider and an id of digits; a GPX key of the upload's own shape. Both are written the positive way, because a negated jsonpath filter over a missing member and a missing JSON key both read as unknown, which a CHECK lets through.
- *One field per service, which takes what the club has.* In «Traseul», after the route link: «Garmin Connect: linkul sau codul de încorporare» and «Strava: linkul sau codul de încorporare». A pure parser per service (`events/domain/route-maps.ts`) reads the link (`strava.com/routes/<id>`; `connect.garmin.com/modern|app|embed/course/<id>`) or the embed code exactly as the share menu gives it, and keeps only the id and, for Strava, `data-style`, `data-map-hash` and `data-token`, each on a strict pattern. Any other attribute, any other host, another script, another element, an id with a letter, an over-long token: refused, naming the box. The pasted text is never stored and never rendered. The box shows the stored map back as the link, or as Strava's placeholder rebuilt from the stored values when there is a token or a view, so a second save never drops them.
- *On the page: tabs, a press per map, a link per service.* Under «Traseul» (`#route`): with two services, the tabs «Garmin Connect» | «Strava», Garmin first as the owner listed them, each with its mark (Strava's, §61; a watch glyph for Garmin Connect, not Garmin's logo), 44 px. One service alone has no tabs. Each panel holds «Arată harta pe …», the sentence «Harta se încarcă de la Strava când apeși; Strava vede adresa ta IP.» (and Garmin's), and «Deschide în …», a link built from the id. The press is the house's facade (§69, §266, §403): a native `<details>` rendered on the server, its iframe lazy inside, so nothing is fetched from either service until the visitor opens it. A tab switch loads nothing.
- *The iframe, built on the server.* Garmin's is its embed address for the id. Strava's is the address Strava's `embed.js` would have built, read from that script on 2026-10-11: `/route/<id>`, the style, `fromEmbed=false` and the token as the query; a namespace, this site's origin and the map's view in the fragment. The page's path and title, which the script also passes, are left out. Sandboxed to scripts, same-origin, popups and popups escaping the sandbox; `referrerpolicy="strict-origin"`; a fixed height, 420 px on a phone, 548 px wider, rather than Strava's height messages, which would need a script on our page.
- *The tabs are one small client island* (`RouteMapTabs`): the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, with roving focus and the arrow keys, Home and End. The panels are the server's, passed as children, and the island hides all but the chosen one by CSS on a data attribute. Rendered with the first tab chosen, so with scripts off the Garmin panel shows with its link and the GPX still downloads. Radio-input CSS tabs were refused: a radio group is not a tablist, and a screen reader would announce the wrong thing.
- *The GPX is a file the club uploads* (`/api/admin/route-gpx`, only `canEditEventFields`, the route field's own rule, asked on the server). It is checked for what it is, never by the extension or the browser's type: UTF-8 text, an optional prolog, the root `<gpx>` (a namespace prefix allowed, a `<!DOCTYPE>` refused), closed at the end; at most 4 MB, because a request to a function on the host carries at most 4.5 MB. It is stored as given under `<env>/route-gpx/<uuid>/<name>.gpx`. The storage adapter's `put` gains an optional `contentDisposition`, which R2 keeps with the object, so the file downloads under its own name as `application/gpx+xml`; `/api/media` gives the same headers in the local and fake modes. The page draws «Descarcă traseul (GPX)» with the file's name and size under the maps, whether or not there is a map. The editor's island (`RouteGpxField`) uploads on choice and posts the answer with the event's one save; «Scoate fișierul» empties it.
- *Deleted when nothing names it, and never swept.* The file is no `media_assets` row, so the pictures' sweep never sees it. A save that replaces or removes it, and an event's erasure, delete the object once no event row names its key: a series' dates and a duplicate share one object. A file uploaded and never saved stays in the store unread. That is a few hundred kilobytes, and the price of not holding the upload inside the save's request.
- *The section exists for a map or a file alone.* «Traseul» was drawn only with a description in the reader's language. It is now drawn with a description, a map or a GPX (`hasRouteSection`). That one rule moves the route's links into it, points the facts' route row at it and gives the emails their deep links, so the page, the preview, the facts and the emails still agree. The route link is not drawn when it is the very Strava route the Strava tab opens.
- *Privacy.* The notice's template now says, beside the YouTube sentence, that a route's map from Strava or Garmin Connect loads only when pressed, and only then does the service receive the IP address and may set its cookies. The feature is not gated on the club approving it (the YouTube precedent); §639 tells the administrators the template moved.

**Refused.** Loading `embed.js` or any provider script. Storing or rendering the pasted HTML. An iframe that loads with the page, or a thumbnail facade, which is itself a request to the provider. A GPX checked by its extension alone. A GPX link to a file elsewhere in place of the upload (the «Linkuri și fișiere» kind stays for that). A Garmin logo copied into the site. Holding the upload until the save, which would put a 4 MB file through the editor's Server Action and its 1 MB limit.

**Erasure and the edges (review round).** The ordinary Administrator delete releases the GPX exactly as the hard delete does: the key is read from the deleted row inside the transaction and handed to the release after the commit, which keeps the object while another date or a duplicate names it. The Garmin iframe check keeps no title and no presentation attribute, so it accepts any title without markup characters and `style`, `scrolling`, `allow`, `referrerpolicy` and `allowtransparency` beside the seven it already read; an `on*` handler, `srcdoc`, `sandbox` and anything else are still refused. A GPX counts toward «Traseul» only where storage is configured, the same condition the download row is drawn under, so an environment without storage never shows an empty heading. Strava's `data-units` and `data-full-width` are accepted and dropped: the map is always metric and its default width, the club's setting is not carried. Open follow-up: a GPX uploaded and then replaced before the save, or uploaded in an editor closed without saving, stays in the store, since no sweep covers `route-gpx/`; a maintenance pass listing the prefix and deleting keys no event names is the remedy, and is not built.

**Tests.** Unit: `events/route-maps.test.ts` (each accepted shape, the hostile ones, the iframe address, the editor's round trip, the lenient reader, the duplicate route link), `events/route-gpx.test.ts` (the checks, the key, the name, the headers, the posted value), `events/route-maps-render.test.ts` (the tabs' roles, the closed disclosures, the links from the ids, the single-service panel, the GPX row, the section for a file alone, the editor's closed line and order). Integration: `cms/route-maps-and-gpx.test.ts` (saved from the pastes, cleared per box, refused naming the box, the CHECKs, a repeat, a series edit and a duplicate, the upload's rights and checks, the download's headers, another environment's key refused, the object kept while a date names it and deleted after, the erasure by hard delete and by ordinary delete, the sweep). E2e: `route-maps.spec.ts`, both projects, on a production build. The browser's request listener sees no request to either service before the press. One press loads Strava's map only, the tabs work by keyboard, and the GPX downloads under its name.

**Not verified.** The iframes are built to the services' published shapes and tested against a stand-in. No live Strava or Garmin map was loaded: the repository is public and the owner's ids are not used. One look at QA with a real route settles whether the sandbox lets each map draw. If one does not, widening the sandbox is a one-line change in `RouteMapPanel.tsx`.

**Review round: where the upload lives, and what a series save lets go.** The owner looked for the GPX upload on the «Traseul (GPX)» row of «Linkuri și fișiere» («Păi da, dar aici am doar un link»), not in «Traseul». So the file field moved to that card, above the rows, and a row of kind «Traseul (GPX)» carries «Încarcă fișierul în loc de link»: a `<label>` for the same file input (`ROUTE_GPX_INPUT_ID`), so it opens with no script and the one hidden `event.routeGpx` still carries the value; «Traseul» keeps the two map boxes. The data, the save and the page are unchanged; the closed line of «Linkuri și fișiere» counts the file («GPX»), and «Traseul»'s names only the maps. A series save with scope following or all writes the saved date's `routeGpx` over every date it reaches, so `applyToSeries` now hands back the GPX keys it overwrote on those dates and the save passes them, with this date's old key, to the post-commit release, which deletes each object no date still names; before, a date that held a different file (after an earlier «from this date» change) left that object with no holder and never deleted. `hasRouteSection` and `hasRouteMedia` take `storageConfigured` from the caller instead of reading the environment, so `route-section.ts` stays pure and a client importer cannot pull the server's environment schema into its bundle; the editor's section map takes the same flag as an optional field of its data.
changelogLine: - **Strava and Garmin Connect maps, and a GPX file, on «Traseul»** — paste a route's link or the embed code the service gives; the page shows «Garmin Connect» | «Strava» tabs, each with its link and its map loaded only when the visitor presses, and «Descarcă traseul (GPX)» under them from a file the club uploads in «Linkuri și fișiere», above the rows or on the GPX row; nothing is asked of Strava or Garmin before the press, and no script of theirs ever runs. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given an event with a Strava route and a Garmin Connect course, when its page renders, then «Traseul» shows the tabs «Garmin Connect» | «Strava» (Garmin first, `role="tablist"`, each tab 44 pixels tall, the first chosen), each panel holding «Arată harta pe …» as the summary of a closed `<details>` whose lazy, sandboxed iframe is built from the stored id alone, the sentence that says the service sees the IP address when pressed, and «Deschide în …» linking to the route on the service; with one service there are no tabs; no provider script is on the page, and the browser makes no request to either service until the visitor presses, when only that map loads (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event with an uploaded GPX, when its page renders, then «Traseul» exists even without a description or a map and shows «Descarcă traseul (GPX)» / «Download the route (GPX)» under the maps, with the file's name and size, at least 44 pixels tall, linking to the stored file, which is served as `application/gpx+xml` with `Content-Disposition: attachment` under the file's own name (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the «Traseul» card, when the organizer pastes a Strava route's link or Strava's embed code, or a Garmin Connect course's link or Garmin's embed code, then the save keeps only the id and, for Strava, the style, the map's view and the token, each on a strict pattern, never the pasted text; a paste with another host, another attribute, a script, an id with a letter or an over-long token is refused naming its box and nothing is written; an empty box clears that service; a series edit, a repeat and a duplicate carry the maps; the database refuses a third service or an id off its pattern whatever writes it (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the «Linkuri și fișiere» card, when an Administrator uploads a GPX (above the rows, or by «Încarcă fișierul în loc de link» on a «Traseul (GPX)» row), then the server accepts it only from a role that may change the event and only as an XML document whose root is `<gpx>`, at most 4 MB, whatever its extension, and stores it as given; the event's save records it and a series and a duplicate carry it; «Scoate fișierul», a replacement — on this date or written over another date by a series save —, or the event's erasure deletes the stored file once no event names it, and the pictures' sweep never deletes it (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
